title: Context Graphs for Explainable, Decision-Aware AI Agents — Andreas Kollegger & Zaid Zaim, Neo4j
talk_summary: The speakers argue that agents need context graphs storing short-term state, long-term entities, and explicit rules/policies so they can make explainable decisions. They present a decision workflow that separates option generation from authority, uses risk/reversibility analysis, and records reasoning as precedent.

takeaways.what_they_do: They split decision-making into a focused agent that only proposes alternatives with pros/cons, then a separate agent with authority ranks/acts or escalates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This agent's job, only thing would be to like actually come up with a proposal of some alternatives

takeaways.what_they_do: They save the decision, reasoning process, considered and rejected options, and actions into the graph so future agents can retrieve them as precedent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: record the entire reasoning process, what you considered, what you didn't consider

takeaways.what_they_do: They feed agents local framing plus global business rules and prior decisions, balancing consistency against reasons to overrule precedent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there are global rules, both the hard and soft rules of a business

takeaways.what_they_do: Before acting, they classify the reference class, reversibility, cost of being wrong, and what value is being maximized; serious or irreversible decisions get more analysis.
A decision agent either acts if it has authority, or escalates to a higher-privilege agent or human when uncertain or unauthorized.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Either act or don't act, let somebody else make the call.
